name: Gale-Verdance
description: Gale-Verdance is a world of rolling emerald plains and jagged mountain ridges, where winds never truly cease. The sky shifts between pale silver and deep cerulean as storm fronts race across the horizon, dragging curtains of warm rain behind them. Vast rift valleys slice through the lowlands, their walls choked with tangled vegetation that sways and roars in the constant gales.

Standing on the surface feels like being caught inside a living bellows. The air is thick with the scent of wet earth and crushed chlorophyll, and the wind carries a low harmonic drone as it funnels through the mountain passes. Nights bring a brief lull, during which bioluminescent mosses paint the valley floors in pale green constellations.

Early survey teams noted that the storm patterns follow an uncanny regularity, as if governed by some planetary-scale mechanism buried deep beneath the crust. A research outpost was established near the largest rift to study the phenomenon, but three expeditions into the deeper caverns have returned with conflicting data and missing equipment. An automated beacon on the northern plateau broadcasts a repeating signal that predates any known colonial presence.

Gale-Verdance's abundant flora and clean atmosphere make it a prime candidate for agricultural colonization, yet the wind speeds routinely exceed two hundred kilometers per hour during storm surges. Any settlement must be built to withstand forces that would shred conventional structures. The mystery of the beacon and the rhythmic storms draws xenoarchaeologists and thrill-seekers in equal measure, though the planet has a way of humbling those who underestimate its fury.
